narrative_purpose: Makes the 26-hour problem physical rather than numerical: a human sleeping compartment shown across successive local days, its occupant's rest sliding steadily out of step with what the window says, so free-running reads as a lived condition instead of an arithmetic result.
subject: A vertical sequence of five identical narrow sleeping berths inside a sealed human habitat, stacked as a column of repeated frames representing five successive local days. Each berth holds the same sleeping human figure under a thin blanket, and each has the same small window beside the bunk. Down the sequence, two things change in opposite directions: the light in the window shifts progressively - from local night, through deep pre-dawn, into full local daylight - while the sleeper's posture stays identically asleep in every frame. In the last frame the window is bright with day while the figure sleeps on, and a small overhead panel of cold artificial habitat light glows in every frame, unchanging.
scene: The interior of a cramped, utilitarian sealed habitat berth, repeated five times as a vertical strip, with the alien daylight visible only through the window.
camera: The identical fixed side-on view of the berth in all five frames, so only the window light and nothing else appears to change.
light: Constant cold artificial overhead light inside every berth; the window light cycling from dark indigo through cold pre-dawn grey to pale bright exterior day down the sequence.
palette: Cold grey-white habitat interior, void-indigo through pale grey-cyan in the windows, one restrained amber indicator on the overhead panel, no warm skin tones emphasised.
style: Painterly naturalist sequence plate, hand-painted texture, deliberately repetitive framing.
detail_level: Crisp on the window light and the sleeping figure in each frame; the berth interior consistent and slightly plain so the only visible variable is the light outside.
composition: Five equal horizontal frames stacked in a vertical column with thin dark gutters, identical interior geometry in each, window on the same side throughout, 9:16 portrait.
consistency_notes: Cold human-habitat palette deliberately opposed to the warm bioluminescent forest plates in this chapter - the visual argument is that this room refuses the local world.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no clock faces, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon or anime style
